The Chicago area broke a record high for Oct. 12 that stood for nearly two decades.

Tyler Pasciak LaRiviere/Sun-Times file

Share

The Chicago area shattered a record high that stood for nearly two decades Monday.

The high at O’Hare Airport reached 88 degrees — four degrees higher than the previous record for Oct. 12, set in 2008, according to the National Weather Service.

“In this particular case, we had a pretty pronounced ridge with the jet stream across the eastern United States, and this allowed warmer air to surge further north,” said Jake Petr, a meteorologist with the weather service.

Tuesday is expected to be the last day of above-normal temperatures, with highs in the upper 70s, before dipping back into the 60s Wednesday, according to the weather service.

“Today is really the last warm day for this week before we start to cool down into the weekend,” Petr said.

It’s been hotter this late in October, but not by much, with a high of 89 degrees on Oct. 14, 1975 (it was 88 degrees the day before).

The much higher monthly record, however, still stands — 94 degrees on Oct. 6, 1963.
